mean: struggling hard to cope with something

story.text: In Buddhism the four sufferings are birth, old age, sickness and death. The eight add four more: parting from those you love, meeting those you hate, not getting what you seek, and the suffering of the five aggregates that make up body and mind. Together they stand for all the pain of human life; everyday Japanese uses the phrase for a hard struggle with something.

mean: adapting flexibly to the situation at hand
lit: facing the moment, responding to the change

use.how: Usually 臨機応変に + verb (対応する, 動く) or 臨機応変な対応/判断: a person adjusting what they do to what actually happens, instead of sticking to the plan.

near.diff: 当意即妙 is a quick, apt reply or remark on the spot; 臨機応変 is adjusting actions or plans to the situation.

cue: The projector died mid-talk, so the speaker switched to the whiteboard and finished without missing a beat. How did they handle it?

bad.why: It praises sensible adjustment to circumstances. For someone whose views keep shifting, say kimagure na hito or kangae ga korokoro kawaru.
